annotations.description: Node.js event-loop p99 lag has been sustained above 0.5s (normal is 10-70ms). The process is saturated with CPU/synchronous work and is starting to respond slowly to ALL requests — health checks, gRPC, and HTTP alike. This is the LEADING INDICATOR of the event-loop-saturation crashloop pattern (e.g. the prod bkout-one-workflow-backend EmitWorkflowEvent surge, ~3.9k/min, that saturated the single-threaded loop). Istio LEAST_REQUEST load balancing will route NEW traffic away from a lagging pod (it accumulates in-flight requests), which buys time — but sustained lag across pods means the whole service is hot and needs intervention before it crashloops.
annotations.resolution: In SigNoz, chart nodejs_eventloop_lag_p99_seconds alongside request rate for {{ $labels.job }} in {{ $labels.namespace }}. If it's a traffic/event surge (check EmitWorkflowEvent / queue depth), scale replicas or apply backpressure at the source. If it's one pod, LEAST_REQUEST should shed it and it may self-recover — watch container restarts for the crashloop tipping point. Do NOT just restart pods blindly: confirm the upstream driver (event surge, a hot sync code path, GC pressure) or it recurs.
